item.title: API Gateway in a Cloudflare Worker
item.author: bibby@bibs.codes (James Bibby)
item.description: I have been working on some CloudFlare Workers for a number of different things: serving SPAs from S3, adding special headers to certain requests, geo-redirection… and a question came up about our URL structure at work. We have a microservice architecture with domain based routing. service-a.site.com, service-b.site.com, etc. This is a pretty standard routing when using platforms like Kubernetes, Mesosphere, Swarm, etc, but it gets in the way of the performance enhancements offered by HTTP/2 persistent connections in modern browsers.

item.title: About Me

item.description: Overview Hi 👋 I’m (James) Bibby and I write code. I write highly scalable web applications and services. I usually code in Go these days; sometimes in Java, JavaScript, Ruby, Python, or C. I usually store my data in Postgres and Redis; sometimes I use Dynamo, Mongo or MySQL. I build software platforms on AWS (sometimes Azure or Google Cloud) managed with Terraform and Ansible, and my infrastructure is always code.
